newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Tollway should halt planned raises - lawmaker.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Tollway should halt planned raises - lawmaker.

text.p: Illinois State Toll Highway Authority executives should suspend consideration of proposed raises until lawmakers address the agency's budget this fall, a state representative said Monday.

Rep. Jeff Schoenberg, D-Evanston, said the Toll Authority's consideration of executive raises as lawmakers meet to determine whether the agency should face more scrutiny is "a prime example of why we need greater oversight and accountability of the authority's spending practices."
Toll Authority officials said Monday the agency had hired the Hay Group for $98,000 beginning in May 1996 to assess job classifications and compensation for its 450 non-union employees.
A "working draft" of the study rejected by the Toll Authority concluded executives were underpaid, spokesman David Loveday said.
The earliest the Toll Authority would consider raises would be late autumn, Loveday said.
Hay Group had made a similar study in 1989 and was hired again because the Toll Authority had undergone reorganizations since then, Loveday said.
A Cook County judge in May held that the Toll Authority practice of budgeting toll revenues without oversight of the governor or lawmakers violated the state constitution.
Judge Stephen Schiller gave the Toll Authority until Dec. 15 to address the issue or be enjoined from all expenditures except debt service on nearly $1 billion of outstanding debt.

Toll Authority officials, and First National Bank Chicago as trustee of all outstanding debt, have appealed Schiller's ruling and General Assembly committees opened a joint hearing into the agency's spending practices earlier in July.
Schoenberg serves as chairman of one of the two House appropriations committees conducting the hearing.
Moody's Investor's Service, Standard & Poor's and Fitch Investor's Service have raised credit concerns over the bondholdings.
Officials from several other debt-issuing state agencies also have said they are watching the case closely to determine whether it could affect them as well.
